subject: Follow-up: throughput & token economics from today's demo
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@streamlineai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: throughput & token economics from today's demo

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the items we said we'd follow up on: 

1) Your estimated monthly token volume: you mentioned a range that varies by feature — canonical numbers you gave were 40M tokens/month for search snippets and up to 150M tokens/month when the generative assistant is enabled for power users.

2) Target unit economics: you indicated a budget envelope that targets roughly $800–$1,200 per 1M tokens for inference (including embeddings + generation), with an internal goal to keep runtime costs under $1.0M per month at peak.

3) Batching & concurrency assumptions: you described a mostly steady stream of short requests (avg prompt+response ~120 tokens) with occasional spikes during product events (concurrency up to ~600 simultaneous active sessions). You also expect long-tail sessions that reuse context (chat threads) which could benefit from KV cache reuse and prefix caching.

Next steps we agreed:
- I’ll route the numbers to our pricing team and return a back-of-envelope cost model tuned for continuous batching and your expected concurrency profile.
- Lauren will propose an initial deployment config (batching windows, max concurrency per model replica, fallback model variants) and estimated SLOs.
- Marcus will attach a short spreadsheet with throughput / token-cost sensitivity.

Attachments: throughput-estimates.xlsx (baseline calc).

Would you and procurement be comfortable sharing a high-level MRP or expected ramp schedule (Q2-Q4) so we can size Dedicated vs Hosted pricing? If not now, a ballpark weekly traffic curve will do.

Thanks — Jon

--
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Park <olivia@streamlineai.com>

Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & token economics from today's demo

Thanks Jonas — great walkthrough. A few clarifications and additional detail: 

- Token breakout: Search snippets (~40M/mo) are ~95% embeddings read ops; Assistant (if enabled) would be ~150M/mo where generate tokens are ~70% (completion) and ~30% are prompt tokens.
- Budget: the $800–$1,200 / 1M tokens is what product leadership has penciled; procurement will need line items for dedicated capacity and a hosted fallback.
- Ramp: conservative plan is 10% weekly growth after pilot, target baseline in 3 months. Spike scenario: a marketing push could increase concurrent sessions to 900+ for up to 6 hours.

For the deep-dive, please include: expected tail-latency under continuous batching, how prefix/KV cache helps chat threads, and a recommended quantization profile for cost vs quality.

Procurement loop: procurement@streamlineai.com — they will be on the next thread for contracting.

Olivia
Head of Product, StreamlineAI

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@streamlineai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & token economics from today's demo

Hi Olivia — looping in a few concrete numbers so you can evaluate against your $/1M token target. High-level notes below and attached a short SLO/pricing sketch (see SOW-v0.3.pdf for contract framing).

Summary: given your workload mix (heavy short requests + some deeper generation):
- Continuous batching expectations: we assume a 10–25 ms batching window on our hosted runtime for low-latency pathways; effective batching for short requests typically reduces per-token compute by ~18–35% depending on request size and model choice.
- Concurrency handling: we model baseline concurrency at 200 active streams with autoscale to 900 for spikes. For Dedicated pools we recommend per-replica reserved concurrency of 250 with an autoscale buffer for bursts — this preserves latency SLOs while letting batching run efficiently.
- Unit economics back-of-envelope (using your 120-token avg request):
  • Hosted (mixed model): ~ $950 / 1M tokens (mid-case) when leveraging continuous batching + kv-prefix cache for chat reuse.
  • Dedicated (reserved GPU + optimized quantized weights): ~ $620 / 1M tokens (mid-case) with aggressive quantization and higher amortization of GPU costs.

Notes on assumptions:
- We assume 70% of requests are < 200 tokens (short path), which benefits most from continuous batching.
- KV/prefix cache reuse reduces total generated tokens by ~8–12% in chat-heavy flows (we modeled 25% of sessions as chat threads with medium context reuse).
- These are initial estimates; we'll refine once we have a 7-day traffic sample and a handful of representative prompts.

Next steps we propose:
1) Short technical deep-dive (60 min) with your infra team to validate concurrency and spike tolerance.
2) Provide a 7-day ingestion for us to run a simulated cost run (we'll return a token-by-token cost breakdown).
3) Draft a pilot SOW based on Dedicated + Hosted fallback — attached SOW-v0.3.pdf for internal review.

Marcus attached throughput-estimates.xlsx with sensitivity scenarios (see column "batch_window_ms" and "replica_count"). Marcus — can you flag any additional knobs before we share these with procurement?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
